sources.entry: Rulesync by dyoshikawa - A Node.js CLI tool that automatically generates configs (rules, ignore files, MCP servers, commands, and subagents) for various AI coding agents. Rulesync can convert configs between Claude Code and other AI agents in both directions.

summary.one_liner: Rulesync is a Node.js CLI that generates AI coding tool configuration files (rules, ignore files, MCP servers, commands, subagents, skills) from a unified set of source rule files, and can convert configs between tools.
summary.what_it_does: Rulesync reads unified AI rule files from a .rulesync/ directory and generates the native configuration files for many AI coding tools, with selective generation by target and feature. It can also import existing tool configs (such as CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or .github/copilot-instructions.md) into .rulesync/. A convert command translates configs directly from one tool to others without writing .rulesync/ files. The README lists a large set of supported tools across rules, ignore, MCP, commands, subagents, skills, hooks, permissions, and checks. It also includes a fetch command for installing official skills. Several targets are marked deprecated or end-of-life, and the README documents how each is still handled.
use_cases: keep one set of AI rules in sync across multiple coding assistants
convert Cursor rules to Claude Code or GitHub Copilot
import existing CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules into a unified format
generate MCP server configs for several AI tools at once
install shared AI agent skills into a project
migrate AI tool configuration between vendors
notable: Converts configs directly between AI tools with a convert command, without requiring a .rulesync/ source directory
Supports bidirectional import and export across a large list of AI coding tools
Project-only plugin packaging targets write into existing plugin directories via --output-roots
Documents deprecations and end-of-life status for several targets (Continue, Roo Code, Tabnine CLI, Rovo Dev), with guidance on replacements
Can be installed as a single binary via a curl install script
caveats: The ignore feature is deprecated in favor of permissions, though existing ignore configs remain supported in 14.x
Several targets are deprecated or end-of-life (Continue, Roo Code, Tabnine legacy CLI, Rovo Dev standalone), and remain supported only as frozen-compatibility targets
Plugin targets are excluded from --targets "*" and must be selected explicitly
keywords: one config for many ai agents
